title: FreeViS: Training-free Video Stylization with Inconsistent References
claim: Our method yields richer style detail and fewer propagation errors than prior baselines, across stylization and generation tasks.
layout: 4 quadrant gallery, style/content inputs left, ours versus baseline rows, zoom-in insets
description: A gallery of stylized video frames in two halves. The top half, labeled Video Stylization, shows a style reference (a Chinese ink landscape) and a content frame (a man with a backpack in a forest) on the left. Two rows of four frames each follow: FreeViS on top and AnyV2V* below. A dashed arrow labeled Propagation Error runs beneath, showing the baseline degrading over time. Zoomed insets, outlined in orange for FreeViS and green for AnyV2V*, compare texture detail: FreeViS keeps crisp brush textures and AnyV2V* looks blurry. The bottom half, labeled Stylized Video Generation, has two panels. One pairs a watercolor style with a skateboarder and compares StyleMaster to FreeViS+Wan. The other pairs The Great Wave with a woman vacuuming and compares StyleCrafter to FreeViS+Wan. Text prompts sit on captions at the bottom. The eye goes first to the top forest frames.
caption: Previous works (e.g., AnyV2V [ref]) suffer from propagation errors inherent to their single-reference inputs. Combined with a text-to-video model [ref], FreeViS outperforms existing methods [ref] on stylized video generation.
abstract: Video stylization plays a key role in content creation, but it remains a challenging problem. NaÃ¯vely applying image stylization frame-by-frame hurts temporal consistency and reduces style richness. Alternatively, training a dedicated video stylization model typically requires paired video data and is computationally expensive. In this paper, we propose FreeViS, a training-free video stylization framework that generates stylized videos with rich style details and strong temporal coherence. Our method integrates multiple stylized references to a pretrained image-to-video (I2V) model, effectively mitigating the propagation errors observed in prior works, without introducing flickers and stutters. In addition, it leverages high-frequency compensation to constrain the content layout and motion, together with flow-based motion cues to preserve style textures in low-saliency regions. Through extensive evaluations, FreeViS delivers higher stylization fidelity and superior temporal consistency, outperforming recent baselines and achieving strong human preference. Our training-free pipeline offers a practical and economic solution for high-quality, temporally coherent video stylization. The code and videos can be accessed via https://xujiacong.github.io/FreeViS/
